youtube.title: DR ALISON GOODWIN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Dr Alison Goodwin, a New Zealand GP and patient-rights advocate, about her ongoing investigation into Covid-19 vaccine injuries. Goodwin discusses myocarditis mechanisms and symptoms, disputed death tolls, redacted coroner and MedSafe records, the exclusion of teenagers from post-vaccine monitoring, and what she describes as systemic buck-passing among health authorities. The conversation touches on specific cases, medical tribunals, and the upcoming election's potential influence on accountability. Watch What Officials Knew About Myocarditis Risk for Teens Read RCR's Beyond the Bite full report For the documented evidence and wider timeline, visit ThePeoplesReport.co.nz and ThePeoplesPosition.co.nz For the timeline around 12-15 year olds No longer trusting the 6pm news? youtube.title: PROF MAAN ALKAISI
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Professor Maan Alkaisi, who lost his wife in the 2011 CTV building collapse, about the fatal Mount Maunganui landslide that killed six people during January's extreme rainfall. Drawing parallels between both disasters, Alkaisi discusses ignored engineering reports, a lack of accountability among council leadership, and the pattern of costly inquiries producing little real change, calling for genuine oversight to prevent further preventable loss of life. More from RCR on the Mount Maunganui disaster Sam Uffindell, National MP for Tauranga: Council Under Fire Over Landslide Cameron Luxton, ACT Party MP: Mount Maunganui Tragedy, Local Government & MMP A Political Agenda with Maree Buscke, Ro Edge and David Lynch David Lynch, Advocate: Call for Royal Inquiry into Mount Tragedy Go beyond the 6pm news with RCR Bites — FREE every weekday

youtube.title: UNDER THE HOOD
youtube.summary: Graham “Hoody” Hood reflects on how fear, social media and division fuel conflict, arguing that empathy and genuine conversation are the strongest antidotes. Drawing on personal experiences of defusing hostility and his work in recovery, he makes the case for restoration over retribution, urging people to seek understanding, accountability and common ground to heal families, communities and society.
